summary: All 296 tests pass (0 failures). WP-005 adds 18 integration tests for workspace-orchestrator.ts. All 4 ACs verified: (1) npm test passes, (2) tests use local bare git repo via buildOrigin() with no network calls, (3) filesystem state verified after create/delete/rename with fs.existsSync assertions, (4) both deleteWorkspace and renameWorkspace throw for STABLE workspace.

summary: Reviewed src/tests/workspace-orchestrator.test.ts (18 integration tests) and the supporting workspace-orchestrator.ts, vscode-workspace.ts, and orchestration.types.ts. Code quality is high across all four review dimensions — maintainability, best practices, performance, and future alignment. No blocking issues found.

Architecture is clean: makeFixture() factory eliminates setup boilerplate; buildOrigin() shared read-only origin avoids per-test network calls; makeTempDir() ensures per-test filesystem isolation. Each test has a single focused assertion purpose. Error message pattern assertions (regex) are resilient to minor message wording changes. assert.rejects used correctly for async error paths.

Security guards verified in tests: path-traversal via ../../outside correctly throws, STABLE protection enforced in both delete and rename, self-rename guard tested. Production code validates newId before any I/O to avoid partial-update states — a good defensive pattern that is well-commented.
Two documentation-forward items recorded (non-blocking). No fix-forward changes required.

comments.note: [documentation-forward] renameWorkspace has no test for 'workspace folder does not exist on disk before rename'. The analogous deleteWorkspace case IS tested ('deleteWorkspace succeeds when workspace folder does not exist on disk'). The production code handles this correctly via fs.existsSync guard, but test coverage is asymmetric. A test or a comment explaining the omission would help future contributors.

[documentation-forward] The createWorkspace positive-path tests (e.g. 'creates the workspace folder', 'generates the VS Code workspace file') do not call workspaceManager.create() before invoking orchestrator.createWorkspace(). The class-level docstring states 'The workspace data entry is expected to already exist'. Tests that violate a documented precondition are a future maintenance trap — if enforcement is ever added, these tests will silently break. A brief comment in the test file explaining the intentional omission would eliminate ambiguity.

The deleteWorkspace path-traversal test ('deleteWorkspace validates that target path is under projectsFolder') creates an orchestrator without calling initializeStorage(), relying on the security guard firing before storage is accessed. This is correct today. A brief inline comment noting this ordering dependency would preserve the intent for future readers.

notes: All 4 acceptance criteria met and verified. 18 integration tests cover createWorkspace (7 tests), deleteWorkspace (5 tests), and renameWorkspace (6 tests) with solid edge-case coverage including partial clone failure, path traversal, STABLE protection, and self-rename guard. Two documentation-forward items noted for the Documentation agent: (1) missing renameWorkspace 'folder absent on disk' test or comment, (2) createWorkspace positive tests deviate from documented precondition without explanation.
